newsitem.title: USA: "ZYKLON B" license plate to be recalled in Virginia.
newsitem.headline: "ZYKLON B" license plate to be recalled in Virginia.

text.p: The Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles said on Tuesday a license plate bearing the name of a gas used at German death camps during the Second World War could no longer be used by a state resident.

"We sent out a letter to the individual and advised him that the plate was being recalled," Jeanne Chenault, spokeswoman for the Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles, said. "We supplied him with a regular issue plate."

The letter meant that Ryan Maziarka, 21, the Hampton, Virginia, man identified as the user of the plates, would have to remove tags reading "ZYKLON B", and that the combination of letters would no longer be acceptable for so-called "vanity" plates.
"It will be on file as not issued and not a valid plate," Chenault said.
Maziarka, who can appeal the decision, told the Virginian-Pilot newspaper he was aware of the significance of Zyklon B to the Holocaust -- which he did not believe had occurred.
"I want people to ask me what it (Zyklon B) is, to tell them it's a big lie," he said.

Maziarka had been using the "Zyklon B" plates since January, one of many specialised plates Virginia residents can order for an annual $10 fee. About 12 percent of vehicles in the state have such tags.

The Anti-Defamation League filed a complaint about the license plate on Friday. The state recalled the plate after determining that it violated a restriction on issuing license plates with words that can be considered socially or ethnically disparaging.
Virginia will not issue vanity plates with drug-related or sexually explicit words or profane language, among others.
